method: Read990 additional contiguous result painting lines; static row/header/scrollbar geometry and cache call review.
findings: Scoped-result loop increments list_y by item_h per row, while normal/home loops derive row y from fixed list_y+i*item_h. Common scrollbar code afterwards treats current list_y as top and adds n*item_h again. Scoped scrollbar therefore uses end-of-list as origin; source arithmetic mismatch, not screenshot-qualified.

Thumbnail cache miss invokes load_shell_thumbnail(path,256) synchronously during paint in both normal and scoped results. Cache prune called on insert, actual helper still unread. Shell/IO latency and cancellation unmeasured.
Thumbnail cache keys use path only in these branches, no mtime/identity in lookup. Same-path replacement can retain old thumbnail until eviction; other invalidation paths remain unread.

Scoped section-per-group rendering is guarded by literal false even when starts_section; only first-result-derived global header remains. Group header count code is dead in this path, not evidence of displayed per-source headers.

Content matches get dedicated title/snippet/meta rendering in normal search; scoped mode uses generic description highlighting. Rendering differences do not establish different search matching or file identity.
Long title breadcrumb position uses full measured title width even when title itself ellipsized, so breadcrumb rect can begin beyond right boundary. Actual GDI behavior/layout remains untested.

Filter counts/display result counts reflect candidate list, not exhaustive indexed corpus. Search engine broad cap/outer filters reviewed earlier; UI labels alone do not prove all matching files found.
Image detection is extension-based, not decode validity. No image decoding success/fidelity can be credited from drawing path alone.
limits: No new runtime/tests, visual validation or accepted optimization.
